_comment: SpaceMiT K1 (X60), 8 cores, measured through ModelBlaster's own generated-C kernels (the IREE/merlin execution path is retired). Profiles come from ModelBlaster's profile_writer via PROFILE_OUT_ROOT=<repo>/gen_mb/profile, which is why gen_root is gen_mb and not gen -- gen/profile is the retired IREE tree and mixing the two would compare timings from two different runtimes.
_machines_comment: ONE pool of 8, not cpu_p:4 + cpu_e:4. ingest_xpurt_schedule maps CPU_P#n and CPU_E#n to the n-th registry core OF THE NAMED KIND, and every core in cores/spacemit_k1.json is kind 'rvv' -- so with cpu_p_kind = cpu_e_kind = rvv, CPU_P#0 and CPU_E#0 both resolve to cluster0_core0 (hart 0) and cluster 1 is never used. A single CPU_P pool of 8 maps 1:1 onto harts 0-7.
_capabilities_comment: IME is measured, not assumed: smt.vmadot executes on cores 0-3 and SIGILLs on 4-7 (artifacts/k1_bringup/*/ime_capability_probe.txt). It is a property of cluster-0 cores, never a separate machine -- see xpu-rt/capabilities.py. No ModelBlaster kernel targets it today; see artifacts/k1_run/ime_gate/FINDINGS.md.
_topo_comment: topo_tag_override=true pins every machine combination to the single-core profile. singletons + topo_0 must go together: a multi-hart timing here would credit each core with the whole cluster's throughput. ModelBlaster's K1 runner only ever produces topo_<cpu> profiles for the one core it pinned, so topo_0 is what exists.
